thread:
maya: quick async scrub — what I did / blockers / today
maya: did a pass on the kernel-prefetch PR, added a microbatch counter to the allocator, pushed tests
oscar: saw the counter, thanks. CI flaked once but logs look clean now :+1:
li: re: microbatch counter — did you measure the scheduling jitter with it enabled?
maya: basic run: `./perf/run_sim.sh --profile microbatch --iters 300` gave 2.1ms median jitter, 4.8ms p95 on my laptop; will run fleet smoke later
oscar: nice. can you also run with KV warmup enabled? curious about the cold start tail
maya: yep — KV warmup on yields 1.6ms median, p95 ~3.2ms. attaching quick snippet of the command I used:
```
# local perf run
./perf/run_sim.sh --profile microbatch --iters 300 --kv-warmup --samples 5
```
oscar: great. blocker for me: the batcher occasionally stalls when a slot gets preempted, I have a repro but need help instrumenting slot handoff metrics
li: I can add a small hook to emit slot state transitions (idle->reserved->inflight->done). where do you want the metrics sent? prometheus or local log?
oscar: prometheus is ideal for dashboards, but local logs are ok for the repro trace. maybe both?
li: will do both. PR incoming in ~2 hours, will add a tracer id to correlate across logs
maya: heads-up: I left one TODO in kernel_prefetch.cc about race on the free-list when eviction and reserve happen concurrently — not blocking rollout but should be fixed before we flip the opt-in flag
sam: I can take that TODO after lunch. if it's a simple CAS, I can land it in a follow-up patch. any guidance on preferred pattern?
li: prefer the existing atomic freelist helper (Allocator::try_pop_atomic) — matches our fences. if you need a short chat ping me
sam: will do. also quick ping on code review: @maya can you look at my batching heuristics update? small change to the dynamic batch-sizing logic, tests added
maya: on my list — aiming to review before EOD PST
oscar: perf note: ran a tiny cluster sweep on canary with the microbatch counter and KV warmup; observed 6% p50 latency improvement for short seqs (<=128) and 3% increase in long tail for >1024 when burst factor >2
li: that's expected — microbatching helps steady throughput but can hurt worst-case for long sequences. we should consider adaptive thresholds by seq length
oscar: opened an issue with the numbers and heatmap: https://internal.redwood/issue/RT-4382
maya: thanks. blocker for me: CI integration tests timed out on macOS builder due to flakiness in the env helper, I filed a ticket RT-4383 and disabled the flaky test in the PR to unblock other changes
deploy-bot: deployment queued: canary-2026-03-17-07 (microbatch + kv-warmup), will run health checks for 15m
li: watch the canary dashboards for the next 20m, paying attention to slot handoff rate and batch size distribution
oscar: I'll be watching slot_handoff_total and batch_size_histogram. will post quick notes if anything spikes

oscar: today I'll: 1) finish slot handoff instrumentation, 2) triage canary telemetry, 3) start a short writeup on adaptive thresholds
